name: Yarmouth Chamber Music Festival
nameFr: Festival de Musique de Chambre de Yarmouth
description: A festival of chamber music each autumn in kitchens, chapels, museums and churches across Yarmouth, Pubnico and Clare, Nova Scotia. Presented by the Hear! Here! Society.
about: The goal is not simply to bring great music to Yarmouth. The goal is to build something that lasts. A community where professional musicians want to come, where audiences can encounter chamber music in intimate and unexpected settings, where young musicians can learn from extraordinary artists, and where Yarmouth can become a destination for chamber music in Atlantic Canada.
We believe that great music shouldn’t be confined to big cities or concert halls. It should be something everyone can experience, regardless of age, background, or income.

That’s why this festival isn’t just about concerts. It’s about free performances in schools and long-term care homes, bilingual programming that reflects our Acadian heritage, and open rehearsals held in public spaces where people can experience the creative process up close. It’s about artists meeting audiences. Not from a distance, but in shared spaces, as neighbours.

For ten days each autumn, exceptional musicians become part of the fabric of our community. There are opportunities to encounter them at rehearsals, conversations, discussions and performances — sometimes planned, sometimes spontaneous.

team.name: David Yang
bio: David Yang is an internationally respected violist, chamber musician and artistic director whose collaborations include members of the Borromeo, Brentano, Miró, Tokyo and Vermeer quartets. For 20 years he served as Director of Chamber Music at the University of Pennsylvania. He is also Artistic Director of the Newburyport and Ashburton Chamber Music Festivals and has commissioned dozens of new works.

support.headline: Great music belongs here, not only in big cities, and it’s best shared as neighbours.
text: Every ticket, donation and word of encouragement helps turn a good idea into a lasting tradition.

To support our ongoing efforts to bring more programming like this to Yarmouth and surrounding areas, you can reach out to one of the festival organizers about volunteering or contribute financially. The Hear! Here! Society is a registered non-profit, but we cannot issue charitable tax receipts.
